walkthroughs.body_html:
When overheating, you sweat and skin capillaries dilate.

When cold, you shiver, hairs stand on end, and capillaries constrict to keep warmth in. Both controlled by the hypothalamus.

When dehydrated, the pituitary releases more ADH. ADH makes kidney tubules more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed.

Urine is darker and more concentrated. Negative feedback restores water levels.

FSH matures an egg; oestrogen builds the uterus lining; LH triggers ovulation; progesterone maintains the lining.

Contraceptive pills use oestrogen/progesterone to inhibit FSH.

mcqs.q: How does sweating help cool you down?
options: Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Sweat is cold and directly cools the skin on contact.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Evaporation of sweat absorbs energy (latent heat) from the skin, lowering body temperature.

mcqs.q: What does negative feedback do in homeostasis?
options: It reverses a change in a controlled variable, bringing it back towards the set point.
Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Negative feedback stops the body from responding to any internal change.
Negative feedback makes a process get worse or amplifies the change.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: Sweating removes excess heat by carrying it out as liquid waste.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.
